text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"The retrieved passages do not directly address whether nuclear power reduces carbon emissions.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c2","text":"One retrieved passage is a thesis on coupling wind farms with nuclear power plants.","cited_pids":["bf24b47c7909#1"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Most nuclear power plants are sited on sea coasts because seawater serves as the ultimate heat sink.","cited_pids":["bf24b47c7909#1"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Wind farms depend on good wind resources.","cited_pids":["bf24b47c7909#1"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"The wind-nuclear coupling thesis evaluates benefits and obstacles through case studies but gives no emissions figures.","cited_pids":["bf24b47c7909#2"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"The other retrieved passages concern nuclear effective field theory and pion production in nuclear collisions.","cited_pids":["6f3e7419a5f3#1","85645ea372d7#0"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"No retrieved passage presents evidence on lifecycle emissions, cost, or safety of nuclear power.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c8","text":"No retrieved passage contradicts the idea that nuclear power reduces carbon emissions.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c9","text":"Answering the question well would require sources on lifecycle carbon intensity of nuclear power versus other generation.","cited_pids":[]}]}
